title: Rakesh Srivastava v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Dr Dhananjaya Yeshwant Chandrachud, CJ and Yashwant Varma, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner left to pursue the domestic-connection application under clauses 4.4 and 4.8.
headnote: Mandamus for immediate issue of a domestic electricity connection is refused on the merits where clauses 4.4 and 4.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 already cover the application. The petitioner may pursue that application; the competent authority shall act in accordance with law.
facts: Rakesh Srivastava sought a mandamus that respondent no. 3 issue a domestic electricity connection forthwith at House No. 121 B, Generalganj, Tehsil Sadar, District Mathura. The High Court did not enquire into occupancy, title, or any Code default. After disposal on 4 April 2016, the petitioner obtained an amendment and a correction so that the prayer described the premises as House No. 1218 rather than 121 B.

holding_units.topic: processing of new domestic connection application
holding_units.holding: Clauses 4.4 and 4.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 contain sufficient provisions to cover a request for a domestic connection. The writ petitioner is left to pursue the application, and the competent authority shall take action in accordance with law.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioner is entitled on the merits to a domestic connection at the Mathura premises
not_decided.note: The Court neither granted nor refused the connection; it left the application to be processed under clauses 4.4 and 4.8.
